Definition — Variance, covariance, covariance matrix
Assume finite second moments for the variance and covariance formulas below. $\operatorname{Var}(X)=\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb EX)^2]=\mathbb E[X^2]-(\mathbb EX)^2$; the standard deviation $\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}X}$ has the units of $X$ (noise variance $0.01$ means standard deviation $0.1$), and $\operatorname{Var}(aX+b)=a^2\operatorname{Var}X$. $\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb EX)(Y-\mathbb EY)]$. For a random vector $X\in\mathbb R^n$ with mean $m$,
$$\Sigma=\operatorname{Cov}(X)=\mathbb E\big[(X-m)(X-m)^\top\big],\qquad \Sigma_{ij}=\operatorname{Cov}(X_i,X_j),\qquad \operatorname{Cov}(AX+b)=A\Sigma A^\top .$$
Isotropic noise has $\Sigma=\sigma^2I$: uncorrelated coordinates with the same variance $\sigma^2$ in every direction. The correlation of $X,Y$ with standard deviations $\sigma_X,\sigma_Y\gt0$ is $\rho=\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)/(\sigma_X\sigma_Y)$, the covariance of the standardised variables. It lies in $[-1,1]$ because $0\le\operatorname{Var}\big(\tfrac X{\sigma_X}\pm\tfrac Y{\sigma_Y}\big)=2(1\pm\rho)$, and $\rho=\pm1$ exactly when $Y$ is almost surely an affine function of $X$ (slope of sign $\pm$). In these terms the vector $(X,Y)$ has covariance matrix $\begin{bmatrix}\sigma_X^2&\rho\sigma_X\sigma_Y\\\rho\sigma_X\sigma_Y&\sigma_Y^2\end{bmatrix}$.
Fact — Covariance matrices are positive semidefinite
For every $v\in\mathbb R^n$, $v^\top\Sigma v=\mathbb E\big[(v^\top(X-m))^2\big]=\operatorname{Var}(v^\top X)\ge0$, so $\Sigma\succeq0$ (Primer A). It is positive definite, hence invertible, iff no nonzero combination $v^\top X$ is almost surely constant.

Worked example (ensemble spread). Two ensemble members predict means $\mu_1=(1,0)$ and $\mu_2=(-1,0)$. Their average is $\bar\mu=(0,0)$ and the outer-product estimate $\hat\Sigma=\tfrac12\sum_e(\mu_e-\bar\mu)(\mu_e-\bar\mu)^\top=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix}$ is PSD but singular: the members disagree only along the first axis. With $E$ members in $\mathbb R^n$ this estimate has rank at most $E-1$, so it is singular whenever $E\le n$ and must not be inverted. A fusion rule such as $\big(\tfrac1E\sum_e\Sigma_e^{-1}\big)^{-1}$ needs every member covariance $\Sigma_e$ to be positive definite.

Worked example (averaging over a policy). In a state $s$, action $a_1$ has expected cost $\mathbb E[X\mid a_1]=2$ and action $a_2$ has $\mathbb E[X\mid a_2]=10$. Under $\pi=(0.7,0.3)$ the tower rule gives $\mathbb E[X]=0.7\cdot2+0.3\cdot10=4.4$. Under another policy $\pi'=(0.9,0.1)$ the conditional expectations, a property of the environment, are unchanged and only the weights move: $0.9\cdot2+0.1\cdot10=2.8$. The performance-difference lemma averages the advantage of $\pi$ over the actions of $\pi'$ in exactly this way.

Theorem — Law of total variance
$\operatorname{Var}(X)=\mathbb E\big[\operatorname{Var}(X\mid Y)\big]+\operatorname{Var}\big(\mathbb E[X\mid Y]\big)$: the average spread within groups plus the spread of the group means. Proof. With $\bar X=\mathbb E[X\mid Y]$, the tower rule gives $\mathbb E[X^2]=\mathbb E\big[\mathbb E[X^2\mid Y]\big]=\mathbb E\big[\operatorname{Var}(X\mid Y)+\bar X^2\big]$ and $\mathbb E[X]=\mathbb E[\bar X]$; subtract $(\mathbb E\bar X)^2$ from both sides. $\square$ For vectors, $\operatorname{Cov}(X)=\mathbb E[\operatorname{Cov}(X\mid Y)]+\operatorname{Cov}(\mathbb E[X\mid Y])$.
Definition — Mixture distribution
First draw a label $L$ with $\mathbb P(L=j)=w_j$, then draw $X$ from the component law $p_j$ (mean $m_j$, variance $\sigma_j^2$). Then $X$ has density $p(x)=\sum_jw_jp_j(x)$, mean $\bar m=\sum_jw_jm_j$ and, by total variance, $\operatorname{Var}X=\sum_jw_j\sigma_j^2+\sum_jw_j(m_j-\bar m)^2$.

Worked example (small and large errors). Residuals that are $\mathcal N(0,0.5^2)$ with probability $0.8$ and $\mathcal N(0,3^2)$ with probability $0.2$ (the "80% small, 20% large" option of the Module 15 explorer) have variance $0.8\cdot0.25+0.2\cdot9=2$. Their tail is nothing like that of $\mathcal N(0,2)$: $\mathbb P(|E|\gt5)=0.8\cdot\mathbb P(|Z|\gt10)+0.2\cdot\mathbb P(|Z|\gt\tfrac53)\approx0.019$, against $0.0004$ for the Gaussian with the same variance, while near zero the mixture is more concentrated ($\mathbb P(|E|\gt1)\approx0.18$ against $0.48$). An ensemble of $E$ Gaussian predictions is an equal-weight mixture: its covariance is the average member covariance (aleatoric part) plus the covariance of the member means (epistemic part, the $\hat\Sigma$ of Section 1).

Left: the $n$ calibration scores, the quantile $\hat q$ (index $k=\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil$) and the coverage measured on 2000 fresh test scores. Right: for each $n$, 30 independent calibration sets (grey dots), their mean coverage (blue), the theoretical mean $k/(n+1)$ (dotted) and the band $[1-\alpha,\,1-\alpha+\tfrac{1}{n+1}]$ (green). The score distribution changes $\hat q$, i.e. the size of the prediction set (left), but for continuous scores neither the band nor the spread of the coverage (right). The simulation draws i.i.d. scores, so for $k\le n$ the coverage of a fixed calibration set is $F(s_{(k)})\sim\mathrm{Beta}(k,\,n+1-k)$ whatever the continuous score CDF $F$ is, and switching the distribution only reshuffles the grey dots. For $k=n+1$, i.e. $(n+1)\alpha\lt 1$, $\hat q=\infty$ and the coverage is identically 1, with no spread. The “three standard errors” use the exact beta-binomial variance $p(1-p)(n+1+2000)/(2000\,(n+2))$ of one run, $p=k/(n+1)$, divided by the 30 runs.

Background — Student-t scores and mixtures

The three score distributions are generated from independent standard normals $Z,Z_0,Z_1,Z_2,Z_3$. Gaussian: $|Z|$. Student-t with 3 degrees of freedom: $|Z_0|/\sqrt{(Z_1^2+Z_2^2+Z_3^2)/3}$; the three squared normals in the denominator are the three degrees of freedom, and because the denominator is itself random and occasionally small (a numerator of 1 over a denominator of 0.1 gives a score of 10), very large scores are far more frequent than under Gaussian noise: the distribution has heavy tails. Mixture (Primer C): with probability $0.8$ draw $|0.5Z|$, otherwise $|3Z|$. All three are continuous, so the rank argument and the Beta law of Section 5 hold for each; only the scale and the tail change, and with them the size of the prediction sets.

Background — Beta-binomial variability of the simulated coverage

Let $C$ be the coverage of one calibration set, a random variable, and $\hat C$ its measured coverage on $m=2000$ fresh test scores. For continuous i.i.d. scores and $k\le n$, $C\sim\mathrm{Beta}(k,n+1-k)$ (Section 5) and, given $C$, $m\hat C\sim\mathrm{Bin}(m,C)$: a binomial count whose success probability is itself Beta-distributed, called a beta-binomial count. With $p=k/(n+1)$, $\operatorname{Var}(C)=p(1-p)/(n+2)$ and $\mathbb E[C(1-C)]=\mathbb E[C]-\mathbb E[C]^2-\operatorname{Var}(C)=p(1-p)(n+1)/(n+2)$. The law of total variance (Primer C),

$$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Var}(\hat C)&=\operatorname{Var}\big(\mathbb E[\hat C\mid C]\big)+\mathbb E\big[\operatorname{Var}(\hat C\mid C)\big]\\&=\operatorname{Var}(C)+\frac{\mathbb E[C(1-C)]}{m}\\&=\frac{p(1-p)(n+1+m)}{m(n+2)},\end{aligned}$$

shows that the calibration and test-sampling variances add; standard deviations do not, which is why the readout adds the two variances before taking a square root. Averaging 30 independent runs divides the variance by 30, and the plotted check uses three times the resulting standard error: a simulation diagnostic, not a deterministic band or an exact confidence statement. Example: $n=99$, $\alpha=0.1$, so $k=90$, $p=0.9$, $m=2000$: $\operatorname{Var}(\hat C)\approx0.000936$, and the standard error of a 30-run mean is about $0.0056$.

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set
open scoped NNReal ENNReal BigOperators
namespace SafeLearning.CompleteAppliedGaussianMixtureLaw24
open CompleteAppliedFiniteMixtureMaterial24 CompleteAppliedGaussianCDF
  CompleteAppliedGaussianStandardization

def componentWeight (b : Bool) : ℝ≥0 := if b then 1/5 else 4/5

def componentLaw (b : Bool) : Measure ℝ :=
  if b then gaussianReal 0 9 else gaussianReal 0 (1/4)

def residualLaw : Measure ℝ := finiteMixture componentWeight componentLaw

def absoluteTail (μ : Measure ℝ) (r : ℝ) : ℝ := μ.real {x | r < |x|}

private theorem normalizedWeights : ∑ b, componentWeight b = 1 := by
  norm_num [componentWeight, Fintype.sum_bool]

private instance componentProbability (b : Bool) : IsProbabilityMeasure (componentLaw b) := by
  cases b <;> dsimp [componentLaw] <;> infer_instance

instance residualProbability : IsProbabilityMeasure residualLaw :=
  actual_finite_mixture_is_a_probability_law componentWeight normalizedWeights componentLaw

theorem actual_source_residual_has_finite_second_moment : MemLp id 2 residualLaw :=
  actual_finite_mixture_has_finite_second_moment componentWeight componentLaw id
    (fun b => by cases b <;> exact memLp_id_gaussianReal 2)

theorem actual_source_residual_mean_and_variance :
    (∫ x, x ∂residualLaw) = 0 ∧ variance id residualLaw = 2 := by
  have hm := actual_finite_mixture_mean componentWeight componentLaw id
    (fun b => by cases b <;> exact memLp_id_gaussianReal 2)
  have hv := actual_finite_mixture_variance componentWeight normalizedWeights componentLaw id
    (fun b => by cases b <;> exact memLp_id_gaussianReal 2)
  change (∫ x, x ∂finiteMixture componentWeight componentLaw) = 0 ∧
    variance id (finiteMixture componentWeight componentLaw) = 2
  norm_num [Fintype.sum_bool, componentLaw, componentWeight,
    integral_id_gaussianReal, variance_id_gaussianReal] at hm hv
  exact ⟨hm, hv⟩

theorem actual_source_residual_tail_is_the_weighted_component_tail (r : ℝ) :
    absoluteTail residualLaw r =
      (4/5:ℝ)*absoluteTail (gaussianReal 0 (1/4)) r +
      (1/5:ℝ)*absoluteTail (gaussianReal 0 9) r := by
  simp only [absoluteTail, residualLaw, finiteMixture, Fintype.sum_bool]
  rw [measureReal_add_apply (by simp [Measure.smul_apply]; finiteness) (by simp [Measure.smul_apply]; finiteness)]
  simp [componentWeight, componentLaw]
  ring

theorem actual_standard_gaussian_absolute_tail (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) :
    absoluteTail (gaussianReal 0 1) r = 2*(1-standardCDF r) := by
  let μ := gaussianReal 0 1
  haveI : NullSingletonClass μ := nullSingletonClass_gaussianReal (by norm_num)
  have hset : Iic r \ Iio (-r) = Icc (-r) r := by ext x; simp
  have hd := measureReal_sdiff (μ:=μ) (s₁:=Iic r) (s₂:=Iio (-r))
    (by intro x hx; change x < -r at hx; change x ≤ r; linarith) measurableSet_Iio
  rw [hset, measureReal_congr (Iio_ae_eq_Iic (μ:=μ))] at hd
  change μ.real (Icc (-r) r) = standardCDF r - standardCDF (-r) at hd
  rw [actual_standard_gaussian_cdf_reflection] at hd
  have hc := measureReal_compl (μ:=μ) (s:=Icc (-r) r) measurableSet_Icc
  have he : (Icc (-r) r)ᶜ = {x : ℝ | r < |x|} := by
    ext x; simp only [mem_compl_iff, mem_Icc, mem_setOf_eq]
    rw [← not_le, abs_le]
  rw [he] at hc
  change μ.real {x | r < |x|} = _
  have hu : μ.real univ = 1 := by simp [μ]
  rw [hu] at hc
  linarith

theorem actual_positive_scaled_gaussian_tail (s r : ℝ) (hs : 0 < s) (hr : 0 ≤ r) :
    absoluteTail (gaussianReal 0 (⟨s^2, sq_nonneg s⟩)) r =
      2*(1-standardCDF (r/s)) := by
  have hm := gaussianReal_map_const_mul (μ:=0) (v:=1) s
  simp only [mul_zero, mul_one] at hm
  have he : (fun x : ℝ => s*x) ⁻¹' {x | r < |x|} = {x | r/s < |x|} := by
    ext x; simp only [mem_preimage, mem_setOf_eq, abs_mul, abs_of_pos hs]
    rw [div_lt_iff₀ hs]; rw [mul_comm]
  have hp := map_measureReal_apply (μ:=gaussianReal 0 1)
    (by fun_prop : Measurable (fun x : ℝ => s*x))
    (s:={x | r < |x|}) (measurableSet_lt measurable_const measurable_abs)
  rw [hm, he] at hp
  change absoluteTail (gaussianReal 0 ⟨s^2, sq_nonneg s⟩) r =
    absoluteTail (gaussianReal 0 1) (r/s) at hp
  rw [hp, actual_standard_gaussian_absolute_tail _ (div_nonneg hr hs.le)]

theorem actual_printed_source_tail_formulas :
    absoluteTail residualLaw 5 = (4/5:ℝ)*2*(1-standardCDF 10) +
      (1/5:ℝ)*2*(1-standardCDF (5/3)) ∧
    absoluteTail residualLaw 1 = (4/5:ℝ)*2*(1-standardCDF 2) +
      (1/5:ℝ)*2*(1-standardCDF (1/3)) := by
  have hsmall (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) := actual_positive_scaled_gaussian_tail (1/2) r (by norm_num) hr
  have hlarge (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) := actual_positive_scaled_gaussian_tail 3 r (by norm_num) hr
  have hvs : (⟨(1/2:ℝ)^2, sq_nonneg (1/2:ℝ)⟩ : NNReal) = (1/4 : NNReal) := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    change (1/2:ℝ)^2 = 1/4
    norm_num
  have hvl : (⟨(3:ℝ)^2, sq_nonneg (3:ℝ)⟩ : NNReal) = (9 : NNReal) := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    change (3:ℝ)^2 = 9
    norm_num
  constructor <;> rw [actual_source_residual_tail_is_the_weighted_component_tail]
  · have a := hsmall 5 (by norm_num); have b := hlarge 5 (by norm_num)
    rw [hvs] at a; rw [hvl] at b; rw [a,b]; norm_num; ring
  · have a := hsmall 1 (by norm_num); have b := hlarge 1 (by norm_num)
    rw [hvs] at a; rw [hvl] at b; rw [a,b]; norm_num; ring

end SafeLearning.CompleteAppliedGaussianMixtureLaw24

    (∫ x in (0:ℝ)..r,polynomial48 x)=polynomialIntegral48 r := by
  have ht (i : ℕ) :
      (∫ x in (0:ℝ)..r,(-x^2/2)^i/(i.factorial:ℝ)) =
        (-1/2:ℝ)^i*r^(2*i+1)/((i.factorial:ℝ)*(2*i+1)) := by
    have he : (fun x : ℝ => (-x^2/2)^i/(i.factorial:ℝ)) =
        (fun x => ((-1/2:ℝ)^i/(i.factorial:ℝ))*x^(2*i)) := by
      funext x
      have hz : -x^2/2 = (-1/2:ℝ)*x^2 := by ring
      rw [hz,mul_pow,←pow_mul]; ring
    rw [he,intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul,integral_pow]
    simp; field_simp
  unfold polynomial48 polynomialIntegral48
  rw [intervalIntegral.integral_finsetSum]
  · apply Finset.sum_congr rfl; intro i hi; exact ht i
  · intro i hi
    exact (by fun_prop : Continuous (fun x : ℝ => (-x^2/2)^i/(i.factorial:ℝ))).intervalIntegrable _ _

import Mathlib
set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section
namespace SafeLearning.CompleteAppliedMixtureCovarianceMaterial24
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped ENNReal NNReal BigOperators Matrix.Norms.Elementwise
variable {ι Ω : Type*} [Fintype ι] [MeasurableSpace Ω]
def finiteMixture (w : ι → ℝ≥0) (μ : ι → Measure Ω) : Measure Ω :=
  ∑ i, (w i : ℝ≥0∞) • μ i
private theorem probability_law (w : ι → ℝ≥0) (hw : ∑ i, w i = 1)
    (μ : ι → Measure Ω) [∀ i, IsProbabilityMeasure (μ i)] :
    IsProbabilityMeasure (finiteMixture w μ) := by
  constructor
  simp only [finiteMixture, Measure.finsetSum_apply, Measure.smul_apply,
    measure_univ, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
  exact_mod_cast hw
private theorem weighted_integral (w : ι → ℝ≥0) (μ : ι → Measure Ω)
    (X : Ω → ℝ) (hX : ∀ i, Integrable X (μ i)) :
    (∫ ω, X ω ∂finiteMixture w μ) = ∑ i, (w i : ℝ) * ∫ ω, X ω ∂μ i := by
  rw [finiteMixture, integral_finsetSum_measure
    (fun i _ => (hX i).smul_measure ENNReal.coe_ne_top)]
  simp [NNReal.smul_def, smul_eq_mul]
private theorem mixture_memLp (w : ι → ℝ≥0) (μ : ι → Measure Ω)
    (X : Ω → ℝ) (hX : ∀ i, MemLp X 2 (μ i)) : MemLp X 2 (finiteMixture w μ) := by
  have hs : AEStronglyMeasurable X (finiteMixture w μ) := by
    rw [finiteMixture, ← Measure.sum_fintype]
    exact AEStronglyMeasurable.sum_measure
      (fun i => ((hX i).smul_measure ENNReal.coe_ne_top).aestronglyMeasurable)
  apply (memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq hs).mpr
  rw [finiteMixture, integrable_finsetSum_measure]
  intro i _
  exact ((hX i).smul_measure ENNReal.coe_ne_top).integrable_sq
private theorem component_centered_product (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (X Y : Ω → ℝ) (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) (M N : ℝ) :
    (∫ ω, (X ω - M)*(Y ω - N) ∂μ) =
      covariance X Y μ + ((∫ ω, X ω ∂μ)-M)*((∫ ω, Y ω ∂μ)-N) := by
  have hx := hX.integrable one_le_two
  have hy := hY.integrable one_le_two
  have hxy := hX.integrable_mul hY
  have he : (fun ω => (X ω-M)*(Y ω-N)) =
      (fun ω => X ω*Y ω-N*X ω-M*Y ω+M*N) := by ext ω; ring
  rw [he]
  change (∫ ω, (((X*Y)-(fun ω=>N*X ω))-(fun ω=>M*Y ω)) ω + M*N ∂μ) = _
  rw [integral_add ((hxy.sub (hx.const_mul N)).sub (hy.const_mul M))
    (integrable_const _)]
  rw [integral_sub' (hxy.sub (hx.const_mul N)) (hy.const_mul M),
    integral_sub' hxy (hx.const_mul N)]
  simp only [Pi.mul_apply]
  rw [integral_const_mul, integral_const_mul,
    integral_const, covariance_eq_sub hX hY]
  simp only [probReal_univ, one_smul, Pi.mul_apply]
  ring

theorem actual_finite_mixture_covariance_within_and_between
    (w : ι → ℝ≥0) (hw : ∑ i, w i = 1)
    (μ : ι → Measure Ω) [∀ i, IsProbabilityMeasure (μ i)]
    (X Y : Ω → ℝ) (hX : ∀ i, MemLp X 2 (μ i)) (hY : ∀ i, MemLp Y 2 (μ i)) :
    covariance X Y (finiteMixture w μ) =
      (∑ i, (w i : ℝ)*covariance X Y (μ i)) +
      ∑ i, (w i : ℝ)*
        ((∫ ω, X ω ∂μ i)-(∑ j, (w j : ℝ)*∫ ω, X ω ∂μ j))*
        ((∫ ω, Y ω ∂μ i)-(∑ j, (w j : ℝ)*∫ ω, Y ω ∂μ j)) := by
  let M : ℝ := ∑ j, (w j : ℝ)*∫ ω, X ω ∂μ j
  let N : ℝ := ∑ j, (w j : ℝ)*∫ ω, Y ω ∂μ j
  have hx := weighted_integral w μ X (fun i => (hX i).integrable one_le_two)
  have hy := weighted_integral w μ Y (fun i => (hY i).integrable one_le_two)
  rw [covariance, hx, hy]
  rw [weighted_integral w μ (fun ω => (X ω-M)*(Y ω-N))
    (fun i => (hX i |>.sub (memLp_const M)).integrable_mul (hY i |>.sub (memLp_const N)))]
  simp_rw [component_centered_product _ _ _ (hX _) (hY _), mul_add]
  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  simp only [M, N, mul_assoc]

variable [MeasurableSpace ι] [MeasurableSingletonClass ι]
def labelLaw (w : ι → ℝ≥0) : Measure ι := finiteMixture w (fun i => Measure.dirac i)

theorem actual_covariance_of_component_means_is_the_between_term
    (w : ι → ℝ≥0) (m n : ι → ℝ) :
    covariance m n (labelLaw w) =
      ∑ i, (w i : ℝ)* (m i-∑ j, (w j : ℝ)*m j)*
        (n i-∑ j, (w j : ℝ)*n j) := by
  have hi (f : ι → ℝ) : (∫ i, f i ∂labelLaw w) = ∑ i, (w i : ℝ)*f i := by
    rw [labelLaw, weighted_integral w (fun i => Measure.dirac i) f
      (fun i => integrable_dirac (by simp))]
    simp
  rw [covariance, hi m, hi n, hi]
  simp only [mul_assoc]

def covarianceMatrix {κ : Type*} (X : κ → Ω → ℝ) (μ : Measure Ω) : Matrix κ κ ℝ :=
  fun a b => covariance (X a) (X b) μ

theorem actual_finite_vector_mixture_covariance_matrix
    {κ : Type*} [Fintype κ] (w : ι → ℝ≥0) (hw : ∑ i, w i = 1)
    (μ : ι → Measure Ω) [∀ i, IsProbabilityMeasure (μ i)]
    (X : κ → Ω → ℝ) (hX : ∀ a i, MemLp (X a) 2 (μ i)) :
    covarianceMatrix X (finiteMixture w μ) =
      (∑ i, (w i : ℝ) • covarianceMatrix X (μ i)) +
      covarianceMatrix (fun a i => ∫ ω, X a ω ∂μ i) (labelLaw w) := by
  ext a b
  simp only [Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.smul_apply, covarianceMatrix]
  rw [actual_finite_mixture_covariance_within_and_between w hw μ
    (X a) (X b) (hX a) (hX b), actual_covariance_of_component_means_is_the_between_term]
  simp only [smul_eq_mul]

theorem actual_equal_weight_ensemble_covariance_matrix
    {κ : Type*} [Fintype κ] [Nonempty ι]
    (μ : ι → Measure Ω) [∀ i, IsProbabilityMeasure (μ i)]
    (X : κ → Ω → ℝ) (hX : ∀ a i, MemLp (X a) 2 (μ i)) :
    covarianceMatrix X
      (finiteMixture (fun _ => (Fintype.card ι : ℝ≥0)⁻¹) μ) =
      (1/(Fintype.card ι : ℝ)) • (∑ i, covarianceMatrix X (μ i)) +
      covarianceMatrix (fun a i => ∫ ω, X a ω ∂μ i)
        (labelLaw (fun _ => (Fintype.card ι : ℝ≥0)⁻¹)) := by
  have hc : (Fintype.card ι : ℝ≥0) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_ne_zero
  have hw : (∑ i : ι, (Fintype.card ι : ℝ≥0)⁻¹) = 1 := by
    simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul]
    exact mul_inv_cancel₀ hc
  rw [actual_finite_vector_mixture_covariance_matrix _ hw μ X hX]
  simp only [NNReal.coe_inv, NNReal.coe_natCast, ← Finset.smul_sum, one_div]

end SafeLearning.CompleteAppliedMixtureCovarianceMaterial24

Definition — Variance, covariance, covariance matrix
Assume finite second moments for the variance and covariance formulas below. $\operatorname{Var}(X)=\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb EX)^2]=\mathbb E[X^2]-(\mathbb EX)^2$; the standard deviation $\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}X}$ has the units of $X$ (noise variance $0.01$ means standard deviation $0.1$), and $\operatorname{Var}(aX+b)=a^2\operatorname{Var}X$. $\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb EX)(Y-\mathbb EY)]$. For a random vector $X\in\mathbb R^n$ with mean $m$,
$$\Sigma=\operatorname{Cov}(X)=\mathbb E\big[(X-m)(X-m)^\top\big],\qquad \Sigma_{ij}=\operatorname{Cov}(X_i,X_j),\qquad \operatorname{Cov}(AX+b)=A\Sigma A^\top .$$
Isotropic noise has $\Sigma=\sigma^2I$: uncorrelated coordinates with the same variance $\sigma^2$ in every direction. The correlation of $X,Y$ with standard deviations $\sigma_X,\sigma_Y\gt0$ is $\rho=\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)/(\sigma_X\sigma_Y)$, the covariance of the standardised variables. It lies in $[-1,1]$ because $0\le\operatorname{Var}\big(\tfrac X{\sigma_X}\pm\tfrac Y{\sigma_Y}\big)=2(1\pm\rho)$, and $\rho=\pm1$ exactly when $Y$ is almost surely an affine function of $X$ (slope of sign $\pm$). In these terms the vector $(X,Y)$ has covariance matrix $\begin{bmatrix}\sigma_X^2&\rho\sigma_X\sigma_Y\\\rho\sigma_X\sigma_Y&\sigma_Y^2\end{bmatrix}$.
Fact — Covariance matrices are positive semidefinite
For every $v\in\mathbb R^n$, $v^\top\Sigma v=\mathbb E\big[(v^\top(X-m))^2\big]=\operatorname{Var}(v^\top X)\ge0$, so $\Sigma\succeq0$ (Primer A). It is positive definite, hence invertible, iff no nonzero combination $v^\top X$ is almost surely constant.

Worked example (ensemble spread). Two ensemble members predict means $\mu_1=(1,0)$ and $\mu_2=(-1,0)$. Their average is $\bar\mu=(0,0)$ and the outer-product estimate $\hat\Sigma=\tfrac12\sum_e(\mu_e-\bar\mu)(\mu_e-\bar\mu)^\top=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix}$ is PSD but singular: the members disagree only along the first axis. With $E$ members in $\mathbb R^n$ this estimate has rank at most $E-1$, so it is singular whenever $E\le n$ and must not be inverted. A fusion rule such as $\big(\tfrac1E\sum_e\Sigma_e^{-1}\big)^{-1}$ needs every member covariance $\Sigma_e$ to be positive definite.

Worked example (averaging over a policy). In a state $s$, action $a_1$ has expected cost $\mathbb E[X\mid a_1]=2$ and action $a_2$ has $\mathbb E[X\mid a_2]=10$. Under $\pi=(0.7,0.3)$ the tower rule gives $\mathbb E[X]=0.7\cdot2+0.3\cdot10=4.4$. Under another policy $\pi'=(0.9,0.1)$ the conditional expectations, a property of the environment, are unchanged and only the weights move: $0.9\cdot2+0.1\cdot10=2.8$. The performance-difference lemma averages the advantage of $\pi$ over the actions of $\pi'$ in exactly this way.

Theorem — Law of total variance
$\operatorname{Var}(X)=\mathbb E\big[\operatorname{Var}(X\mid Y)\big]+\operatorname{Var}\big(\mathbb E[X\mid Y]\big)$: the average spread within groups plus the spread of the group means. Proof. With $\bar X=\mathbb E[X\mid Y]$, the tower rule gives $\mathbb E[X^2]=\mathbb E\big[\mathbb E[X^2\mid Y]\big]=\mathbb E\big[\operatorname{Var}(X\mid Y)+\bar X^2\big]$ and $\mathbb E[X]=\mathbb E[\bar X]$; subtract $(\mathbb E\bar X)^2$ from both sides. $\square$ For vectors, $\operatorname{Cov}(X)=\mathbb E[\operatorname{Cov}(X\mid Y)]+\operatorname{Cov}(\mathbb E[X\mid Y])$.
Definition — Mixture distribution
First draw a label $L$ with $\mathbb P(L=j)=w_j$, then draw $X$ from the component law $p_j$ (mean $m_j$, variance $\sigma_j^2$). Then $X$ has density $p(x)=\sum_jw_jp_j(x)$, mean $\bar m=\sum_jw_jm_j$ and, by total variance, $\operatorname{Var}X=\sum_jw_j\sigma_j^2+\sum_jw_j(m_j-\bar m)^2$.

Worked example (small and large errors). Residuals that are $\mathcal N(0,0.5^2)$ with probability $0.8$ and $\mathcal N(0,3^2)$ with probability $0.2$ (the "80% small, 20% large" option of the Module 15 explorer) have variance $0.8\cdot0.25+0.2\cdot9=2$. Their tail is nothing like that of $\mathcal N(0,2)$: $\mathbb P(|E|\gt5)=0.8\cdot\mathbb P(|Z|\gt10)+0.2\cdot\mathbb P(|Z|\gt\tfrac53)\approx0.019$, against $0.0004$ for the Gaussian with the same variance, while near zero the mixture is more concentrated ($\mathbb P(|E|\gt1)\approx0.18$ against $0.48$). An ensemble of $E$ Gaussian predictions is an equal-weight mixture: its covariance is the average member covariance (aleatoric part) plus the covariance of the member means (epistemic part, the $\hat\Sigma$ of Section 1).

Left: the $n$ calibration scores, the quantile $\hat q$ (index $k=\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil$) and the coverage measured on 2000 fresh test scores. Right: for each $n$, 30 independent calibration sets (grey dots), their mean coverage (blue), the theoretical mean $k/(n+1)$ (dotted) and the band $[1-\alpha,\,1-\alpha+\tfrac{1}{n+1}]$ (green). The score distribution changes $\hat q$, i.e. the size of the prediction set (left), but for continuous scores neither the band nor the spread of the coverage (right). The simulation draws i.i.d. scores, so for $k\le n$ the coverage of a fixed calibration set is $F(s_{(k)})\sim\mathrm{Beta}(k,\,n+1-k)$ whatever the continuous score CDF $F$ is, and switching the distribution only reshuffles the grey dots. For $k=n+1$, i.e. $(n+1)\alpha\lt 1$, $\hat q=\infty$ and the coverage is identically 1, with no spread. The “three standard errors” use the exact beta-binomial variance $p(1-p)(n+1+2000)/(2000\,(n+2))$ of one run, $p=k/(n+1)$, divided by the 30 runs.

Background — Student-t scores and mixtures

The three score distributions are generated from independent standard normals $Z,Z_0,Z_1,Z_2,Z_3$. Gaussian: $|Z|$. Student-t with 3 degrees of freedom: $|Z_0|/\sqrt{(Z_1^2+Z_2^2+Z_3^2)/3}$; the three squared normals in the denominator are the three degrees of freedom, and because the denominator is itself random and occasionally small (a numerator of 1 over a denominator of 0.1 gives a score of 10), very large scores are far more frequent than under Gaussian noise: the distribution has heavy tails. Mixture (Primer C): with probability $0.8$ draw $|0.5Z|$, otherwise $|3Z|$. All three are continuous, so the rank argument and the Beta law of Section 5 hold for each; only the scale and the tail change, and with them the size of the prediction sets.

Background — Beta-binomial variability of the simulated coverage

Let $C$ be the coverage of one calibration set, a random variable, and $\hat C$ its measured coverage on $m=2000$ fresh test scores. For continuous i.i.d. scores and $k\le n$, $C\sim\mathrm{Beta}(k,n+1-k)$ (Section 5) and, given $C$, $m\hat C\sim\mathrm{Bin}(m,C)$: a binomial count whose success probability is itself Beta-distributed, called a beta-binomial count. With $p=k/(n+1)$, $\operatorname{Var}(C)=p(1-p)/(n+2)$ and $\mathbb E[C(1-C)]=\mathbb E[C]-\mathbb E[C]^2-\operatorname{Var}(C)=p(1-p)(n+1)/(n+2)$. The law of total variance (Primer C),

$$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Var}(\hat C)&=\operatorname{Var}\big(\mathbb E[\hat C\mid C]\big)+\mathbb E\big[\operatorname{Var}(\hat C\mid C)\big]\\&=\operatorname{Var}(C)+\frac{\mathbb E[C(1-C)]}{m}\\&=\frac{p(1-p)(n+1+m)}{m(n+2)},\end{aligned}$$

shows that the calibration and test-sampling variances add; standard deviations do not, which is why the readout adds the two variances before taking a square root. Averaging 30 independent runs divides the variance by 30, and the plotted check uses three times the resulting standard error: a simulation diagnostic, not a deterministic band or an exact confidence statement. Example: $n=99$, $\alpha=0.1$, so $k=90$, $p=0.9$, $m=2000$: $\operatorname{Var}(\hat C)\approx0.000936$, and the standard error of a 30-run mean is about $0.0056$.

theorem actual_standard_gaussian_absolute_tail (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) :
    absoluteTail (gaussianReal 0 1) r = 2*(1-standardCDF r) := by
  let μ := gaussianReal 0 1
  haveI : NullSingletonClass μ := nullSingletonClass_gaussianReal (by norm_num)
  have hset : Iic r \ Iio (-r) = Icc (-r) r := by ext x; simp
  have hd := measureReal_sdiff (μ:=μ) (s₁:=Iic r) (s₂:=Iio (-r))
    (by intro x hx; change x < -r at hx; change x ≤ r; linarith) measurableSet_Iio
  rw [hset, measureReal_congr (Iio_ae_eq_Iic (μ:=μ))] at hd
  change μ.real (Icc (-r) r) = standardCDF r - standardCDF (-r) at hd
  rw [actual_standard_gaussian_cdf_reflection] at hd
  have hc := measureReal_compl (μ:=μ) (s:=Icc (-r) r) measurableSet_Icc
  have he : (Icc (-r) r)ᶜ = {x : ℝ | r < |x|} := by
    ext x; simp only [mem_compl_iff, mem_Icc, mem_setOf_eq]
    rw [← not_le, abs_le]
  rw [he] at hc
  change μ.real {x | r < |x|} = _
  have hu : μ.real univ = 1 := by simp [μ]
  rw [hu] at hc
  linarith

    absoluteTail (gaussianReal 0 (⟨s^2, sq_nonneg s⟩)) r =
      2*(1-standardCDF (r/s)) := by
  have hm := gaussianReal_map_const_mul (μ:=0) (v:=1) s
  simp only [mul_zero, mul_one] at hm

    ext x; simp only [mem_preimage, mem_setOf_eq, abs_mul, abs_of_pos hs]
    rw [div_lt_iff₀ hs]; rw [mul_comm]
  have hp := map_measureReal_apply (μ:=gaussianReal 0 1)
    (by fun_prop : Measurable (fun x : ℝ => s*x))
    (s:={x | r < |x|}) (measurableSet_lt measurable_const measurable_abs)
  rw [hm, he] at hp
  change absoluteTail (gaussianReal 0 ⟨s^2, sq_nonneg s⟩) r =
    absoluteTail (gaussianReal 0 1) (r/s) at hp
  rw [hp, actual_standard_gaussian_absolute_tail _ (div_nonneg hr hs.le)]

  · have a := hsmall 5 (by norm_num); have b := hlarge 5 (by norm_num)
    rw [hvs] at a; rw [hvl] at b; rw [a,b]; norm_num; ring
  · have a := hsmall 1 (by norm_num); have b := hlarge 1 (by norm_num)

    rw [he,intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul,integral_pow]
    simp; field_simp

  have he : |(∫ x in (0:ℝ)..r,Real.exp (-x^2/2))-polynomialIntegral48 r| ≤ r/1000000000000 := by
    rw [intervalIntegral.integral_sub,actual_degree48_polynomial_integral,

Definition — Variance, covariance, covariance matrix
Assume finite second moments for the variance and covariance formulas below. $\operatorname{Var}(X)=\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb EX)^2]=\mathbb E[X^2]-(\mathbb EX)^2$; the standard deviation $\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}X}$ has the units of $X$ (noise variance $0.01$ means standard deviation $0.1$), and $\operatorname{Var}(aX+b)=a^2\operatorname{Var}X$. $\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb EX)(Y-\mathbb EY)]$. For a random vector $X\in\mathbb R^n$ with mean $m$,
$$\Sigma=\operatorname{Cov}(X)=\mathbb E\big[(X-m)(X-m)^\top\big],\qquad \Sigma_{ij}=\operatorname{Cov}(X_i,X_j),\qquad \operatorname{Cov}(AX+b)=A\Sigma A^\top .$$
Isotropic noise has $\Sigma=\sigma^2I$: uncorrelated coordinates with the same variance $\sigma^2$ in every direction. The correlation of $X,Y$ with standard deviations $\sigma_X,\sigma_Y\gt0$ is $\rho=\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)/(\sigma_X\sigma_Y)$, the covariance of the standardised variables. It lies in $[-1,1]$ because $0\le\operatorname{Var}\big(\tfrac X{\sigma_X}\pm\tfrac Y{\sigma_Y}\big)=2(1\pm\rho)$, and $\rho=\pm1$ exactly when $Y$ is almost surely an affine function of $X$ (slope of sign $\pm$). In these terms the vector $(X,Y)$ has covariance matrix $\begin{bmatrix}\sigma_X^2&\rho\sigma_X\sigma_Y\\\rho\sigma_X\sigma_Y&\sigma_Y^2\end{bmatrix}$.
Fact — Covariance matrices are positive semidefinite
For every $v\in\mathbb R^n$, $v^\top\Sigma v=\mathbb E\big[(v^\top(X-m))^2\big]=\operatorname{Var}(v^\top X)\ge0$, so $\Sigma\succeq0$ (Primer A). It is positive definite, hence invertible, iff no nonzero combination $v^\top X$ is almost surely constant.

Worked example (ensemble spread). Two ensemble members predict means $\mu_1=(1,0)$ and $\mu_2=(-1,0)$. Their average is $\bar\mu=(0,0)$ and the outer-product estimate $\hat\Sigma=\tfrac12\sum_e(\mu_e-\bar\mu)(\mu_e-\bar\mu)^\top=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix}$ is PSD but singular: the members disagree only along the first axis. With $E$ members in $\mathbb R^n$ this estimate has rank at most $E-1$, so it is singular whenever $E\le n$ and must not be inverted. A fusion rule such as $\big(\tfrac1E\sum_e\Sigma_e^{-1}\big)^{-1}$ needs every member covariance $\Sigma_e$ to be positive definite.

Worked example (averaging over a policy). In a state $s$, action $a_1$ has expected cost $\mathbb E[X\mid a_1]=2$ and action $a_2$ has $\mathbb E[X\mid a_2]=10$. Under $\pi=(0.7,0.3)$ the tower rule gives $\mathbb E[X]=0.7\cdot2+0.3\cdot10=4.4$. Under another policy $\pi'=(0.9,0.1)$ the conditional expectations, a property of the environment, are unchanged and only the weights move: $0.9\cdot2+0.1\cdot10=2.8$. The performance-difference lemma averages the advantage of $\pi$ over the actions of $\pi'$ in exactly this way.

Theorem — Law of total variance
$\operatorname{Var}(X)=\mathbb E\big[\operatorname{Var}(X\mid Y)\big]+\operatorname{Var}\big(\mathbb E[X\mid Y]\big)$: the average spread within groups plus the spread of the group means. Proof. With $\bar X=\mathbb E[X\mid Y]$, the tower rule gives $\mathbb E[X^2]=\mathbb E\big[\mathbb E[X^2\mid Y]\big]=\mathbb E\big[\operatorname{Var}(X\mid Y)+\bar X^2\big]$ and $\mathbb E[X]=\mathbb E[\bar X]$; subtract $(\mathbb E\bar X)^2$ from both sides. $\square$ For vectors, $\operatorname{Cov}(X)=\mathbb E[\operatorname{Cov}(X\mid Y)]+\operatorname{Cov}(\mathbb E[X\mid Y])$.
Definition — Mixture distribution
First draw a label $L$ with $\mathbb P(L=j)=w_j$, then draw $X$ from the component law $p_j$ (mean $m_j$, variance $\sigma_j^2$). Then $X$ has density $p(x)=\sum_jw_jp_j(x)$, mean $\bar m=\sum_jw_jm_j$ and, by total variance, $\operatorname{Var}X=\sum_jw_j\sigma_j^2+\sum_jw_j(m_j-\bar m)^2$.

Worked example (small and large errors). Residuals that are $\mathcal N(0,0.5^2)$ with probability $0.8$ and $\mathcal N(0,3^2)$ with probability $0.2$ (the "80% small, 20% large" option of the Module 15 explorer) have variance $0.8\cdot0.25+0.2\cdot9=2$. Their tail is nothing like that of $\mathcal N(0,2)$: $\mathbb P(|E|\gt5)=0.8\cdot\mathbb P(|Z|\gt10)+0.2\cdot\mathbb P(|Z|\gt\tfrac53)\approx0.019$, against $0.0004$ for the Gaussian with the same variance, while near zero the mixture is more concentrated ($\mathbb P(|E|\gt1)\approx0.18$ against $0.48$). An ensemble of $E$ Gaussian predictions is an equal-weight mixture: its covariance is the average member covariance (aleatoric part) plus the covariance of the member means (epistemic part, the $\hat\Sigma$ of Section 1).

import Mathlib
set_option autoImplicit false

namespace SafeLearning.CompleteAppliedMixtureCovarianceMaterial24
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped ENNReal NNReal BigOperators Matrix.Norms.Elementwise
variable {ι Ω : Type*} [Fintype ι] [MeasurableSpace Ω]
def finiteMixture (w : ι → ℝ≥0) (μ : ι → Measure Ω) : Measure Ω :=
  ∑ i, (w i : ℝ≥0∞) • μ i
private theorem probability_law (w : ι → ℝ≥0) (hw : ∑ i, w i = 1)
    (μ : ι → Measure Ω) [∀ i, IsProbabilityMeasure (μ i)] :
    IsProbabilityMeasure (finiteMixture w μ) := by
  constructor
  simp only [finiteMixture, Measure.finsetSum_apply, Measure.smul_apply,
    measure_univ, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
  exact_mod_cast hw
private theorem weighted_integral (w : ι → ℝ≥0) (μ : ι → Measure Ω)
    (X : Ω → ℝ) (hX : ∀ i, Integrable X (μ i)) :
    (∫ ω, X ω ∂finiteMixture w μ) = ∑ i, (w i : ℝ) * ∫ ω, X ω ∂μ i := by
  rw [finiteMixture, integral_finsetSum_measure
    (fun i _ => (hX i).smul_measure ENNReal.coe_ne_top)]
  simp [NNReal.smul_def, smul_eq_mul]
private theorem mixture_memLp (w : ι → ℝ≥0) (μ : ι → Measure Ω)
    (X : Ω → ℝ) (hX : ∀ i, MemLp X 2 (μ i)) : MemLp X 2 (finiteMixture w μ) := by
  have hs : AEStronglyMeasurable X (finiteMixture w μ) := by
    rw [finiteMixture, ← Measure.sum_fintype]
    exact AEStronglyMeasurable.sum_measure
      (fun i => ((hX i).smul_measure ENNReal.coe_ne_top).aestronglyMeasurable)
  apply (memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq hs).mpr
  rw [finiteMixture, integrable_finsetSum_measure]
  intro i _
  exact ((hX i).smul_measure ENNReal.coe_ne_top).integrable_sq
private theorem component_centered_product (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (X Y : Ω → ℝ) (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) (M N : ℝ) :
    (∫ ω, (X ω - M)*(Y ω - N) ∂μ) =
      covariance X Y μ + ((∫ ω, X ω ∂μ)-M)*((∫ ω, Y ω ∂μ)-N) := by
  have hx := hX.integrable one_le_two
  have hy := hY.integrable one_le_two
  have hxy := hX.integrable_mul hY
  have he : (fun ω => (X ω-M)*(Y ω-N)) =
      (fun ω => X ω*Y ω-N*X ω-M*Y ω+M*N) := by ext ω; ring
  rw [he]
  change (∫ ω, (((X*Y)-(fun ω=>N*X ω))-(fun ω=>M*Y ω)) ω + M*N ∂μ) = _
  rw [integral_add ((hxy.sub (hx.const_mul N)).sub (hy.const_mul M))
    (integrable_const _)]
  rw [integral_sub' (hxy.sub (hx.const_mul N)) (hy.const_mul M),
    integral_sub' hxy (hx.const_mul N)]
  simp only [Pi.mul_apply]
  rw [integral_const_mul, integral_const_mul,
    integral_const, covariance_eq_sub hX hY]
  simp only [probReal_univ, one_smul, Pi.mul_apply]
  ring

theorem actual_finite_mixture_covariance_within_and_between
    (w : ι → ℝ≥0) (hw : ∑ i, w i = 1)
    (μ : ι → Measure Ω) [∀ i, IsProbabilityMeasure (μ i)]
    (X Y : Ω → ℝ) (hX : ∀ i, MemLp X 2 (μ i)) (hY : ∀ i, MemLp Y 2 (μ i)) :
    covariance X Y (finiteMixture w μ) =
      (∑ i, (w i : ℝ)*covariance X Y (μ i)) +
      ∑ i, (w i : ℝ)*
        ((∫ ω, X ω ∂μ i)-(∑ j, (w j : ℝ)*∫ ω, X ω ∂μ j))*
        ((∫ ω, Y ω ∂μ i)-(∑ j, (w j : ℝ)*∫ ω, Y ω ∂μ j)) := by
  let M : ℝ := ∑ j, (w j : ℝ)*∫ ω, X ω ∂μ j
  let N : ℝ := ∑ j, (w j : ℝ)*∫ ω, Y ω ∂μ j
  have hx := weighted_integral w μ X (fun i => (hX i).integrable one_le_two)
  have hy := weighted_integral w μ Y (fun i => (hY i).integrable one_le_two)
  rw [covariance, hx, hy]
  rw [weighted_integral w μ (fun ω => (X ω-M)*(Y ω-N))
    (fun i => (hX i |>.sub (memLp_const M)).integrable_mul (hY i |>.sub (memLp_const N)))]
  simp_rw [component_centered_product _ _ _ (hX _) (hY _), mul_add]
  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  simp only [M, N, mul_assoc]

variable [MeasurableSpace ι] [MeasurableSingletonClass ι]
def labelLaw (w : ι → ℝ≥0) : Measure ι := finiteMixture w (fun i => Measure.dirac i)

theorem actual_covariance_of_component_means_is_the_between_term
    (w : ι → ℝ≥0) (m n : ι → ℝ) :
    covariance m n (labelLaw w) =
      ∑ i, (w i : ℝ)* (m i-∑ j, (w j : ℝ)*m j)*
        (n i-∑ j, (w j : ℝ)*n j) := by
  have hi (f : ι → ℝ) : (∫ i, f i ∂labelLaw w) = ∑ i, (w i : ℝ)*f i := by
    rw [labelLaw, weighted_integral w (fun i => Measure.dirac i) f
      (fun i => integrable_dirac (by simp))]
    simp
  rw [covariance, hi m, hi n, hi]
  simp only [mul_assoc]

def covarianceMatrix {κ : Type*} (X : κ → Ω → ℝ) (μ : Measure Ω) : Matrix κ κ ℝ :=
  fun a b => covariance (X a) (X b) μ

theorem actual_finite_vector_mixture_covariance_matrix
    {κ : Type*} [Fintype κ] (w : ι → ℝ≥0) (hw : ∑ i, w i = 1)
    (μ : ι → Measure Ω) [∀ i, IsProbabilityMeasure (μ i)]
    (X : κ → Ω → ℝ) (hX : ∀ a i, MemLp (X a) 2 (μ i)) :
    covarianceMatrix X (finiteMixture w μ) =
      (∑ i, (w i : ℝ) • covarianceMatrix X (μ i)) +
      covarianceMatrix (fun a i => ∫ ω, X a ω ∂μ i) (labelLaw w) := by
  ext a b
  simp only [Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.smul_apply, covarianceMatrix]
  rw [actual_finite_mixture_covariance_within_and_between w hw μ
    (X a) (X b) (hX a) (hX b), actual_covariance_of_component_means_is_the_between_term]
  simp only [smul_eq_mul]

theorem actual_equal_weight_ensemble_covariance_matrix
    {κ : Type*} [Fintype κ] [Nonempty ι]
    (μ : ι → Measure Ω) [∀ i, IsProbabilityMeasure (μ i)]
    (X : κ → Ω → ℝ) (hX : ∀ a i, MemLp (X a) 2 (μ i)) :
    covarianceMatrix X
      (finiteMixture (fun _ => (Fintype.card ι : ℝ≥0)⁻¹) μ) =
      (1/(Fintype.card ι : ℝ)) • (∑ i, covarianceMatrix X (μ i)) +
      covarianceMatrix (fun a i => ∫ ω, X a ω ∂μ i)
        (labelLaw (fun _ => (Fintype.card ι : ℝ≥0)⁻¹)) := by
  have hc : (Fintype.card ι : ℝ≥0) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_ne_zero
  have hw : (∑ i : ι, (Fintype.card ι : ℝ≥0)⁻¹) = 1 := by
    simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul]
    exact mul_inv_cancel₀ hc
  rw [actual_finite_vector_mixture_covariance_matrix _ hw μ X hX]
  simp only [NNReal.coe_inv, NNReal.coe_natCast, ← Finset.smul_sum, one_div]

Definition — Hypothesis test, false alarm, missed detection
A test decides between a null hypothesis $H_0$ (e.g. "the system has not changed") and an alternative $H_1$, rejecting $H_0$ when a statistic $T$ exceeds a threshold $c$. For Gaussian models the posterior and the marginal likelihood are available in closed form (Section 4); non-Gaussian likelihoods, such as binary safe/unsafe labels or censored measurements, need approximations (Laplace, expectation propagation, sampling). Preference data give another likelihood: in the Bradley–Terry model an item with score $r_a$ beats one with score $r_b$ with probability $1/(1+e^{-(r_a-r_b)})$, and the negative log-likelihood of an observed preference is the logistic loss $\log(1+e^{-(r_a-r_b)})$.

If $X$ has density $p$ and $c=\mathbb P(X\in A)\gt0$, then $X$ given $X\in A$ has density $p(x)\,\mathbf 1_A(x)/c$: cut the density to $A$ and renormalise. A truncated Gaussian policy is $\mathcal N(m,s^2)$ conditioned on the admissible action interval; a posterior "truncated to its credible region of mass $c$" is the posterior conditioned on a set $A$ of posterior probability $c$.

Under the untruncated posterior, $\mathbb P(\text{stable})\ge\mathbb P(\text{stable}\cap A)=\mathbb P(\text{stable}\mid A)\,\mathbb P(A)\ge0.95\cdot0.99=0.9405$. 6. “With Probability at Least $1-\delta$”: Union Bounds & Confidence Statements

Start here — Budget failure probability explicitly

A $95\%$ statement about one quantity and a $95\%$ statement about every quantity are different events. Ten failure budgets of $0.005$ add to a total budget of $0.05$. Write the desired event first, then decide how the confidence budget must be shared.

When ready, try the Easy, Medium and Hard practice for this section. For a prerequisite gap, review unions and quantifiers.

Definition — Reading a high-probability guarantee
"With probability at least $1-\delta$, $\mathcal S$" names a random experiment and a good event $G=\{\mathcal S\text{ holds}\}$, and claims $\mathbb P(G)\ge1-\delta$; $\delta$ is the failure probability. Quantifiers written after "with probability" sit inside the event:
$$\underbrace{\mathbb P\big(\forall t,\forall x:\ |f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\le\beta_t\sigma_{t-1}(x)\big)\ge1-\delta}_{\text{uniform: one event covers every round and input}}\qquad\text{vs.}\qquad \underbrace{\forall t,x:\ \mathbb P\big(|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\le\beta_t\sigma_{t-1}(x)\big)\ge1-\delta}_{\text{pointwise}}$$
On the uniform event every decision of the algorithm may rely on the band. The pointwise version says nothing about all rounds at once, nor about an input $x_t$ that the algorithm picked because of the data.
Theorem — Union bound (Boole's inequality)
For any finitely or countably many events, dependent or not, $\mathbb P\big(\bigcup_iA_i\big)\le\sum_i\mathbb P(A_i)$. Proof. $\mathbf 1_{\cup_iA_i}\le\sum_i\mathbf 1_{A_i}$ pointwise; take expectations (Tonelli for countably many terms). $\square$ With failure events $F_i=G_i^c$: $\mathbb P\big(\bigcap_iG_i\big)=1-\mathbb P\big(\bigcup_iF_i\big)\ge1-\sum_i\mathbb P(F_i)$. Giving each of $n$ guarantees failure probability $\delta/n$ makes all of them hold jointly with probability at least $1-\delta$.

Worked example (what joint coverage costs). A two-sided Gaussian band at one point with $\delta=0.05$ needs $\beta=1.96$. For $T=100$ rounds at $\delta/T$ each it needs $\Phi^{-1}(1-0.00025)=3.48$; for $T=10^4$, $4.56$: the price grows only like $\sqrt{\log T}$. If the per-step failures were independent with probability $0.001$, joint success over $100$ steps would be exactly $0.999^{100}=0.905$ against the union bound's $0.9$: barely conservative, and the union bound stays valid under dependence, where the product formula does not. The same logic turns per-step chance constraints into a joint one: $\mathbb P(x_t\notin C)\le\delta$ for each $t$ does not give $\mathbb P(\exists t\le T:\ x_t\notin C)\le\delta$, but $\mathbb P(x_t\notin C)\le\delta/T$ for each $t$ does.

Anytime budgets. To cover all $t=1,2,\dots$ at once, spend a summable sequence: $\delta_t=\frac{\delta}{t(t+1)}$ gives $\sum_{t\ge1}\delta_t=\delta\sum_{t\ge1}\big(\frac1t-\frac1{t+1}\big)=\delta$ by telescoping; $\delta_t=\delta/\pi_t$ with $\pi_t=\pi^2t^2/6$, so that $\sum_t\pi_t^{-1}=1$, does the same via $\sum_t1/t^2=\pi^2/6$. For $\delta=0.05$ and $\delta_t=\delta/(t(t+1))$, a two-sided Gaussian band needs $\beta_t=\Phi^{-1}(1-\delta_t/2)=2.24,\ 3.51,\ 4.57,\ 5.45$ at $t=1,10,100,1000$.

Definition — Confidence interval versus credible interval
A confidence interval at level $1-\delta$ is a procedure mapping data to $[L(\mathcal D),U(\mathcal D)]$ such that $\mathbb P_\theta(L\le\theta\le U)\ge1-\delta$ for every fixed value of the unknown $\theta$; the probability is over repetitions of the experiment, and a computed interval either contains $\theta$ or not. Examples: $\bar y\pm1.96\,\sigma/\sqrt N$ for a Gaussian mean with known $\sigma$; $\bar X\pm\sqrt{\ln(2/\delta)/(2N)}$ for $[0,1]$-valued data (Hoeffding). A credible interval is Bayesian: $\mathbb P(\theta\in[L,U]\mid\mathcal D)\ge1-\delta$ under the posterior, with $\theta$ random and the data fixed.

There are $19$ calibration scores and one future score. Assume all $20$ scores are jointly exchangeable and distinct almost surely. A prediction rule accepts the future point when its score is at most the $18$th smallest calibration score. Find its marginal acceptance probability. Why need this not be $90\%$ for each subgroup?

5. Conformal Prediction for Safe Planning and Control

Randomized smoothing certifies a classifier’s decision. Conformal prediction (CP) certifies a prediction set: with a small calibration sample it turns any heuristic uncertainty score into a set that contains the truth with prescribed probability, for any data distribution. In this section $\alpha\in(0,1)$ is the miscoverage level and $\delta$ is the failure probability in the control application.

Algorithm 3: Split conformal prediction (Angelopoulos & Bates)
  1. Choose a nonconformity score $s(x,y)\in\mathbb R$: large when the model’s prediction at $x$ disagrees with $y$ (e.g. $|y-\hat f(x)|$ for regression; $1-\hat f_y(x)$ for classification, with $\hat f_y(x)=e^{z_y}/\sum_j e^{z_j}$ the softmax probability of class $y$ computed from the model’s logits $z_j$ at $x$, Primer E).
  2. On a calibration set $(X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n$ not used for training, compute $s_i=s(X_i,Y_i)$.
  3. Let $\hat q$ be the $\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil/n$ empirical quantile of $s_1,\dots,s_n$: sort the scores and take the $k$-th smallest with $k=\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil$ ($\hat q=+\infty$ if $k\gt n$; $\lceil r\rceil$ is the smallest integer $\ge r$).
  4. For a new input, output $\mathcal C(X_{\rm test})=\{y:\ s(X_{\rm test},y)\le\hat q\}$.
Theorem — Marginal coverage of split conformal prediction (Vovk et al.; Angelopoulos & Bates, Theorem 1 and Theorems D.1–D.2)
Fix the score rule before calibration. If, conditional on training, $(X_1,Y_1),\dots,(X_n,Y_n),(X_{\rm test},Y_{\rm test})$ are exchangeable (i.i.d. suffices; Primer C), then $$ \mathbb P\big(Y_{\rm test}\in\mathcal C(X_{\rm test})\big)\ \ge\ 1-\alpha . $$ If in addition the scores have a continuous joint distribution (no ties almost surely), then also $$ \mathbb P\big(Y_{\rm test}\in\mathcal C(X_{\rm test})\big)\ \le\ 1-\alpha+\frac{1}{n+1}. $$ The probability is over the calibration data and the test point jointly (marginal coverage).

/-- Any three equally likely retained atoms become equiprobable after conditioning.
The retained-event mass is derived by true finite measure additivity. -/
theorem actual_three_equal_retained_outcomes_have_conditional_probability_one_third
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSingletonClass Ω]
    (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (s : Finset Ω) (hs : s.card = 3)
    (q : ℝ) (hq : 0 < q) (hm : ∀ i ∈ s, μ.real {i} = q) (i : Ω) (hi : i ∈ s) :
    (μ[| (s : Set Ω)]).real {i} = 1/3 := by
  classical
  have hsum : μ.real (s : Set Ω) = 3*q := by
    rw [← sum_measureReal_singleton]
    calc
      (∑ j ∈ s, μ.real {j}) = ∑ _j ∈ s, q :=
        Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j hj => hm j hj)
      _ = 3*q := by simp [hs]
  have hsubset : ({i} : Set Ω) ⊆ (s : Set Ω) := singleton_subset_iff.mpr hi
  have h := congrArg ENNReal.toReal (cond_apply s.measurableSet μ ({i} : Set Ω))
  rw [inter_eq_right.mpr hsubset] at h
  simp only [ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_inv, ← measureReal_def] at h
  rw [h, hm i hi, hsum]
  field_simp [ne_of_gt hq]
  <;> ring

theorem actual_conditioning_has_the_cut_and_normalized_density
    {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] (ν : Measure α) (p : α → ℝ≥0∞)
    (hp : Measurable p) (A : Set α) (hA : MeasurableSet A) :
    (ν.withDensity p)[|A] = ν.withDensity
      (fun x => p x * A.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ≥0∞)) x / (ν.withDensity p) A) := by
  have hf : (fun x => p x * A.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ≥0∞)) x /
      (ν.withDensity p) A) = ((ν.withDensity p) A)⁻¹ • A.indicator p := by
    funext x
    by_cases hx : x ∈ A <;> simp [hx, div_eq_mul_inv, mul_comm]
  rw [hf, withDensity_smul _ (hp.indicator hA),
    withDensity_indicator hA, ← restrict_withDensity hA]
  rfl

theorem actual_random_variable_conditioning_pushes_forward_to_its_conditional_law
    {Ω α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace α]
    (μ : Measure Ω) (X : Ω → α) (hX : Measurable X)
    (A : Set α) (hA : MeasurableSet A) :
    (μ[|X ⁻¹' A]).map X = (μ.map X)[|A] := by
  change ((μ (X ⁻¹' A))⁻¹ • μ.restrict (X ⁻¹' A)).map X =
    ((μ.map X) A)⁻¹ • (μ.map X).restrict A
  rw [Measure.map_smul _ hX.aemeasurable,
    ← Measure.restrict_map hX hA, Measure.map_apply hX hA]

theorem actual_positive_density_region_gives_a_true_normalized_conditional_law
    {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] (ν : Measure α) (p : α → ℝ≥0∞)
    (hp : Measurable p) [IsProbabilityMeasure (ν.withDensity p)]
    (A : Set α) (hA : MeasurableSet A) (hc : 0 < (ν.withDensity p).real A) :
    IsProbabilityMeasure (ν.withDensity
      (fun x => p x * A.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ≥0∞)) x / (ν.withDensity p) A)) ∧
      (∀ᵐ x ∂(ν.withDensity p)[|A], x ∈ A) := by
  have hn : (ν.withDensity p) A ≠ 0 := by
    intro hz
    have : (ν.withDensity p).real A = 0 := by simp [measureReal_def, hz]
    linarith
  rw [← actual_conditioning_has_the_cut_and_normalized_density ν p hp A hA]
  exact ⟨cond_isProbabilityMeasure hn, ae_cond_mem hA⟩

theorem actual_nested_conditional_bounds_need_no_independence
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (S A : Set Ω) (hA : MeasurableSet A) (p c : ℝ)
    (hp : 0 ≤ p) (hc : 0 ≤ c)
    (hcond : p ≤ (μ[|A]).real S) (hmass : c ≤ μ.real A) :
    p * c ≤ μ.real (S ∩ A) ∧ p * c ≤ μ.real S := by
  have hprod : (μ[|A]).real S * μ.real A = μ.real (S ∩ A) := by
    have h := congrArg ENNReal.toReal (cond_mul_eq_inter hA S μ)
    simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_mul, ← measureReal_def, inter_comm A S] using h
  have h : p * c ≤ μ.real (S ∩ A) := by
    rw [← hprod]
    exact mul_le_mul hcond hmass hc measureReal_nonneg
  exact ⟨h, h.trans (measureReal_mono inter_subset_left)⟩

theorem actual_literal_truncated_stability_lower_bound_is_9405_over_10000
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (S A : Set Ω) (hA : MeasurableSet A)
    (hcond : (95 : ℝ) / 100 ≤ (μ[|A]).real S)
    (hmass : (99 : ℝ) / 100 ≤ μ.real A) :
    (9405 : ℝ) / 10000 ≤ μ.real S := by
  have h := (actual_nested_conditional_bounds_need_no_independence μ S A hA
    (95/100) (99/100) (by norm_num) (by norm_num) hcond hmass).2
  norm_num at h ⊢
  exact h

theorem actual_hyperparameter_and_function_bounds_have_product_and_union_floor
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (B F : Set Ω) (hB : MeasurableSet B) (δ₁ δ₂ : ℝ)
    (hδ₁ : 0 ≤ δ₁) (hδ₂ : 0 ≤ δ₂) (hu₁ : δ₁ ≤ 1) (hu₂ : δ₂ ≤ 1)
    (hbox : 1-δ₁ ≤ μ.real B) (hband : 1-δ₂ ≤ (μ[|B]).real F) :
    (1-δ₁)*(1-δ₂) ≤ μ.real (B ∩ F) ∧
      1-δ₁-δ₂ ≤ μ.real (B ∩ F) := by
  have h := (actual_nested_conditional_bounds_need_no_independence μ F B hB
    (1-δ₂) (1-δ₁) (by linarith) (by linarith) hband hbox).1
  have hprod : (1-δ₁)*(1-δ₂) ≤ μ.real (B ∩ F) := by
    simpa only [inter_comm F B, mul_comm (1-δ₂) (1-δ₁)] using h
  refine ⟨hprod, le_trans ?_ hprod⟩
  nlinarith [mul_nonneg hδ₁ hδ₂]

    {Ω α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace α]
